summary: Frances Wood is a scholar of sinology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Newnham College and Peking University before serving at the British Library from circa 1977 to 2013.
Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Francesca Fremantle studied at SOAS University of London from 1966 to 1971 and under Chögyam Trungpa from circa 1971 to 1987.

Francesco Sferra is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Raffaele Torella. He has held appointments at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" as professor (circa 2002) and director (circa 2020), and at University of Naples Federico II.
Francis Brinkley, who worked in Japanology, studied at Royal School Dungannon and held a post at the University of Tokyo from circa 1878 to 1881.

Francis Buchanan-Hamilton was an Edinburgh-educated physician and naturalist who studied under John Hope. He served in the Bengal Medical Service (1794–1815) and as director of the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden (1814–1815).

Francis Gladwin worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was a founding member of The Asiatic Society (circa 1784–1812) and served as professor of Persian at Fort William College circa 1801–1805.

Francis Harold Cook, a specialist in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He served as a professor at the University of California, Riverside, and chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research in 1999.
Francis N. J. works in Indology and history and archaeology. He earned a master's at the University of Calicut and completed doctoral studies under M. R. Raghava Varier, attested in 2002.

Francis Vincent Tiso works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Cornell, Harvard, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary, he has taught Tibetan Buddhism at the Pontifical Gregorian University and held visiting posts at Sapienza University of Rome.

Francis Wilford was an Indology and history and archaeology scholar who was a fellow member of The Asiatic Society (circa 1790–1822) and secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Francis William Bain was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. Educated at Westminster School and Christ Church, he served as Professor of History and Political Economy at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from circa 1892 to 1919.

Francis Woodman Cleaves worked in sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Dartmouth, Harvard, and under Paul Pelliot, and served as a professor at Harvard University from 1941 to 1980.

Francis X. Clooney specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Fordham and the University of Chicago, he taught at Boston College (1984–2005) and was appointed Parkman Professor of Divinity at Harvard University in 2005.

Francisco García Ayuso was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Munich from circa 1868 to 1871, working under Martin Haug between 1869 and 1871.

Francisco Varela worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies, earning degrees from the University of Chile and Harvard. He held posts at the University of Chile, CNRS, Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital, and the University of Paris, and co-founded the Mind and Life Institute.

Franciscus Verellen is a sinology and religious studies scholar educated at Hamburg, Oxford, and EPHE under Kristofer Schipper. He served as Director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1991–2021) and taught at EPHE and Columbia.

Frank E. Reynolds was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who spent his career at the University of Chicago, serving as professor from circa 1967 to 2001 and emeritus professor from 2001 to 2019.
Frank F. Conlon is an Indology and history scholar who studied at the University of Minnesota (1969) and served as a professor at the University of Washington from circa 1968 to 2005.

Frank J. Hoffman works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and completed his doctorate under Stewart Sutherland, having also studied under Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, and others.

Frank J. Korom is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed graduate studies at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 1990) and serves as a professor at Boston University (attested 2005).
